raw_text:
Independent review of run r-20260929T103734405948-llac-occupancy-override-shared at head ab2faca57495372eb638a6fb468d56a5dec84054 against base 533155f97e744755783e552dbb5ab41c8f05b375, the section-21 node that carries the shared occupancy target through the environment override. imas_ambix/agent/router.py's DEFAULT_AUTO_OCCUPANCY_TARGET stops binding the unresolved module constant lane.DEFAULT_OCCUPANCY_TARGET -- which reads 0.90 whatever the environment says -- and binds LaneCapacity.OCCUPANCY_TARGET, the attribute the lane estimator resolves through read_occupancy_target() at import. The comment above the binding is rewritten to state that mechanism, and tests/test_agent_lane_shared_occupancy_target.py gains one test that sets IMAS_AMBIX_LANE_OCCUPANCY_TARGET to 0.7, re-imports both modules, and asserts the estimator target, the memory-rule default and the gate's settings field all read 0.7 with the two targets identical.

Goal fidelity. Section 21 requires one occupancy target read by the lane estimator and the router's memory rule, with IMAS_AMBIX_LANE_OCCUPANCY_TARGET still winning. The predecessor node met that at the default and left the override state open; this node closes it at the field the memory rule actually divides by, verified by this review under the override in separate processes per tree: at head the estimator target and the memory-rule default both read 0.7 and are the same object, and router._GenerationGate(None).settings().occupancy_target reads 0.7, while at base the same probe reads estimator 0.7 against memory-rule 0.9 with identity False. Nothing else in the tree reads the unresolved constant: the occupancy target appears only as LaneCapacity.OCCUPANCY_TARGET (lane.py:145 resolved at import; lane.py:792 publishing it in the document) and the router's two uses of its new binding (router.py:220 the settings field default; router.py:464 the gate payload default), so the two figures an operator moves are now the same figure.

Independent verification. Both arms were re-run by this review under the shared project interpreter, each log header naming the revision, the tree, the module under test as imported and the resolved working directory. Head arm at ab2faca5 inside the reviewed worktree: the node's own declared four-file gate, 47 passed, exit 0, imas_ambix.agent.router resolving inside the reviewed worktree and printing 0.9 for both figures with no override set (review-head-gate.log); the serving-interpreter parse check passed and ruff check --no-cache imas_ambix tests printed all checks passed (review-head-parse-ruff.log). Base arm: a scratch copy of the reviewed tree at /tmp/llac-occ-override-base carrying the base revision's router.py with the reviewed test file kept at head, where the new test is the only failure -- 1 failed, 46 passed, exit 1, pytest reading assert 0.9 == 0.7 at tests/test_agent_lane_shared_occupancy_target.py:132 (review-base-gate.red.log). That is the same reading the reviewed node's own negative-control log records, whose first line repeats its declared mutation string verbatim. The reviewed node's gate log and this review's head arm agree figure for figure.

Record. The reviewed manifest is read whole: status complete, commit ab2faca5, the three changed paths, the gate results, both test logs, negative_control_log as a bare absolute path -- the shape whose absence from the predecessor's manifest the stored review records as a finding -- with its note quoting the scratch edit's restoration, and baseline_suite and after_suite both reading none because this run was dispatched unarmed. Two defects, one cosmetic in the landed tree and one in the run's evidence: the committed fragment ends at </section> with no trailing newline, and the manifest's own arms cannot answer whether the run added failures, so this record carries the count derived from this review's two arms. The guard is durable rather than incidental: the identity assertion compares two floats that came from different code paths, so a later re-tuning of the default to the override value cannot satisfy it by literal coincidence (float('0.7') is 0.7 is False).
